denied_material_classes: empirical results not present in admitted sources
source_snapshot.coverage_note: Bounded scoping corpus for conceptual positioning and novelty-risk assessment; not exhaustive and not proof of novelty.

search_directions: human-AI co-creation with artifacts and relational ontology
software and self-evolving agent feedback loops
inclusion_rules: include primary papers, peer-reviewed proceedings, author manuscripts, or normative standards with direct conceptual relevance
include recent nearest-neighbor frameworks that explicitly model artifacts in human-AI co-creation
include empirical or formal work for attribution, incentive, and gaming boundary conditions
record the actual reading level and do not treat metadata-only discovery as evidentiary support
exclusion_rules: exclude popular summaries when a primary source is available
exclude sources used only for naming similarity
exclude unverified claims from hidden drafts or implementation plans
exclude production mechanism selection from Phase A
literature_scope.stop_rule: Stop when every substantive cluster has at least two admitted sources except a normative-standard or method-foundation cluster, and at least two recent nearest neighbors explicitly including artifacts have been found; this is sufficient for Draft 0 novelty-risk assessment, not a systematic or exhaustive review.
out_of_scope: legal determination of ownership or compensation rights
selection of a production economic mechanism

constructs.name: human-agent-artifact coevolution
constructs.definition: A coupled process in which humans and agents generate variations, artifacts retain selected changes through lineage, and later use conditions subsequent evolution.

constructs.name: governed artifact lineage
constructs.definition: Versioned continuity with explicit derivation, attribution, association, and revision relations that preserves behavior-defining changes.

constructs.name: provenance-aware contribution
constructs.definition: A contribution representation that distinguishes ideas, code, curation, testing, and governance-relevant acts with traceable attribution.

constructs.name: downstream utility observability
constructs.definition: The capacity to observe post-acceptance usage or value signals without treating them as sufficient evidence of entitlement.

constructs.name: economic feedback closure
constructs.definition: A provenance-aware link from accepted contribution and downstream utility signals to later resource availability for subsequent evolution, without selecting a production mechanism.

concept_model.feedback_loop: Human and agent variation -> artifact acceptance and lineage retention -> usage/value observability -> resource-feedback question for subsequent evolution -> new variation.

claims.statement: Distributed cognition treats artifacts and technical environments as constitutive parts of cognition and coordination.

counterarguments.note: LLM relation label: Tension with artifact-minimum-unit co-creation frame

claims.statement: PROV-O provides an established ontology for entities, activities, agents, derivation, attribution, association, and revision.
End-user development and meta-design support participation in artifact adaptation, evolution, and sharing.
Community attribution systems can make non-code contributions more visible than commit-only measures.
Data Shapley is a principled attribution family under a specified utility function, but not a general solution across heterogeneous software contributions.
Informal rewards can alter contribution behavior, making causal evaluation of incentives necessary.
Software evolution is already theorized as a long-running feedback phenomenon.
Self-evolving agent frameworks center interaction data, environment feedback, and optimizers, but do not center human governance and persistent artifact lineage.
Tensional-field relational ontology is a close neighbor because it models humans, AI, creative artifacts, and provenance-related flows in one relational network.
Human-AI co-creation literature already treats artifact as part of the minimum analyzable unit.
Sybil resistance remains a boundary condition for any contribution or usage signal.
Reward hacking is a general threat to any measurable value signal used for allocation or control.
Design science requires purposeful artifact construction and evaluation; a Phase A conceptual frame is not yet a completed design-science contribution.
Participatory AI work distinguishes observable participation from substantive decision authority.
Human-AI coevolution has prior naming and framing, so novelty cannot rest on the phrase alone.
The defensible contribution is a narrower integration: governed artifact lineage plus provenance-aware observability plus a future research question about resource-feedback closure.

counterarguments.note: LLM relation label: Artifact already treated as constitutive in nearest neighbors

claims.statement: If artifact lineage and acceptance are made explicit, then contribution visibility will improve relative to commit-only baselines.

counterarguments.note: LLM relation label: Visibility does not imply authority or value

needed_evidence: Comparative study of contribution visibility under explicit lineage vs commit-only controls

variables.operational_definition: presence of explicit artifact-lineage and acceptance annotations
visibility of non-code contributions in attribution records
variables.measure: share of non-code contributions surfaced and rater-recognized

operationalization.test_method: controlled comparative corpus study with blinded raters
operationalization.falsification_condition: No statistically meaningful improvement in non-code contribution visibility over baseline

claims.statement: If resource feedback is contemplated before robust identity and gaming safeguards, then signal distortion will increase.
needed_evidence: Adversarial evaluation of signal gaming under shadow-mode observability

variables.operational_definition: exposure to provisional resource-feedback observability without added safeguards

variables.measure: gaming rate, mismatch between observed signals and independent audits

operationalization.falsification_condition: Distortion does not increase under the exposed condition

contradictions.statement: Artifact inclusion is not a sufficient novelty claim because artifacts already appear in distributed cognition and co-creation frameworks.
Any allocation-linked framing conflicts with the need to avoid selecting a production mechanism in Phase A.

nearest_neighbors.differentiator: Treats governed artifact lineage and resource-feedback question as narrower than general relational co-creation.
nearest_neighbors.excluded_overlap: Does not claim artifact-inclusive relational modeling itself is new.
nearest_neighbors.uncertainty: Boundary between lineage governance and broader co-creation ontology remains thin.

nearest_neighbors.differentiator: Adds explicit lineage-retention and downstream resource-feedback hypotheses rather than artifact membership alone.
nearest_neighbors.excluded_overlap: Does not claim the artifact-as-unit move is new.
nearest_neighbors.uncertainty: Artifact minimum-unit framing may already cover part of the proposed construct set.

nearest_neighbors.differentiator: Uses coevolution as prior framing but ties it to governed artifact lineage and future resource-feedback questions.
nearest_neighbors.excluded_overlap: Does not claim coevolution terminology is novel.
nearest_neighbors.uncertainty: Novelty likely rests on integration rather than conceptual invention.

gaps: No direct primary evidence on a tested economic closure for AI-native software evolution.

No direct validation that the proposed construct set is minimally sufficient.

entries.candidate_contribution: A narrower integration of governed artifact lineage, provenance-aware observability, and downstream resource-feedback questions for AI-native software evolution.
entries.uncertainty: Overlap remains with artifact-inclusive co-creation ontologies; novelty depends on the resource-feedback question and explicit lineage-retention emphasis.

entries.candidate_contribution: Formal separation of contribution visibility from governance authority and from economic entitlement.
entries.uncertainty: Likely synthesis rather than new theory.

entries.candidate_contribution: A shadow-mode observability and attribution substrate as a pre-mechanism evaluation environment.
entries.uncertainty: Needs evidence that observability helps without inducing false confidence.

entries.candidate_contribution: A falsifiable agenda linking lineage completeness, attribution fidelity, and gaming resistance.
entries.uncertainty: Novel only if mechanism-agnostic and empirically discriminative.

threat_model.coverage_statement: Threat coverage is conceptual and Phase A only; no operational sanctions, reward rules, or deployment path are specified.

threats.description: One actor presents many identities to inflate contribution or usage signals.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Treat as a boundary condition for signal interpretation; require identity-assurance hypothesis testing.
needed_evidence: Identity-resistance test under simulated multi-identity submission

threats.description: Multiple actors coordinate to amplify each other’s contributions or downstream-value signals.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Model as a coalition-risk case in future adversarial evaluation.

threats.description: Signals are attached to an identity that did not perform the contribution.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Separate identity assertion from provenance assertion in the conceptual model.

threats.description: Observed downstream usage is artificially inflated.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Treat usage as an observable, not as entitlement evidence.

threats.description: Actors omit contributions or value signals to avoid scrutiny or obligation.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Explicitly compare reported versus independently observed traces.

threats.description: Only favorable lineage segments or contribution evidence are exposed.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Require lineage completeness as a future-evaluation variable.

threats.description: Retroactive alteration of artifact history or derivation claims.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Treat immutable lineage as an invariant and future audit question.

threats.description: Low-effort claiming of others’ ideas before substantive contribution.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Keep idea attribution distinct from acceptance and utility.

threats.description: Long-lived, finely partitioned claims generate cumulative complexity and inequity.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Do not define entitlements in Phase A; treat as an unresolved future concern.

threats.description: A small subset of actors controls framing, visibility, or future decisions.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Separate observable participation from governance authority and require external review.

threats.description: Presence in the trace is mistaken for decision power or legitimacy.
threats.phase_a_treatment: State explicitly that visibility does not imply authority.

threats.description: Actors optimize measurable signals while subverting intended contribution or utility.
threats.phase_a_treatment: Keep resource feedback in shadow-mode research questions and adversarial tests only.

boundary_conditions.statement: Identity assurance is required before interpreting contribution and usage signals as independent.
Visibility of participation does not imply substantive decision authority.
Allocation-like signals are vulnerable to optimization against the metric itself.
Phase A must not specify currency, token, weights, thresholds, emission, burn, transfer, payout, royalty, ownership share, or automatic reward/sanction.
Artifact lineage alone is insufficient to establish novelty because prior work already formalizes provenance and artifact-centered co-creation.

counterarguments.statement: The framework may be a recombination of established ideas in distributed cognition, provenance, and participatory co-creation rather than a new conceptual contribution.
Attribution or reward-like observability can distort behavior and thereby undermine the signals the framework seeks to use.
Participation data may be measurable without being governance-relevant, so the framework could overstate the link between contribution signals and authority.
The agent-evolution literature already explains feedback-driven adaptation, so the added artifact-centered layer must demonstrate more than descriptive richness.

limitations.statement: No production economic mechanism is selected or evaluated.
Novelty is calibrated only against the admitted nearest-neighbor set, not proven exhaustively.
The framework remains conceptual; no empirical validation is claimed.
Contribution valuation is not generalized across all artifact types or communities.
Governance authority and entitlement remain intentionally underspecified.

research_agenda.question: Does explicit artifact lineage improve contribution visibility relative to commit-only baselines?
needed_evidence: Comparative corpus study across projects using lineage-rich and lineage-poor contribution representations

research_agenda.question: Can provenance-aware observability distinguish accepted contribution from downstream utility without collapsing the two?
Under what conditions does signal gaming increase when resource feedback is introduced?
needed_evidence: Adversarial experiments, Sybil-resistance tests, and reward-hacking probes

research_agenda.question: What minimum provenance schema is sufficient for governed artifact lineage in AI-native software evolution?
Does separating observable participation from substantive governance authority improve interpretability of co-creation analytics?
needed_evidence: Expert review across participatory AI and governance studies

research_agenda.question: Which boundary conditions prevent causally invalid inferences from contribution or usage signals?
needed_evidence: Identity assurance, confounding, and selection-bias analysis
